messages:
elaine: heads up — since 03:00 UTC we've seen a ~3x spike in preemptions for the asia-south1 spot GPU pool. autoscaler keeps provisioning nodes that die before kubelet finishes register. link to graph: https://grafana.internal/r/spot-preemptions :grimacing:

samir: ugh. are the preemptions concentrated to a single instance type/zone?

elaine: mostly n1-standard + a2-family in asia-south1-a/b. eviction waves last ~90s, nodes often never reach Ready.

kai: two quick ideas: increase the cluster-autoscaler `--max-node-provision-time` to 10m so CA waits a bit longer before treating as failed, and add a short-lived warm pool of untainted nodes to absorb scheduling while spots churn.

samir: +1 on max-node-provision-time, but that only hides the symptom. we should also change our drain strategy: set a graceful-drain-window so pods get a longer SIGTERM window (for long init containers).

elaine: any kubectl snippets for the taint workaround? we want a small prewarm pool that can accept GPU jobs but not be scheduled for long-running users.

kai: create a tiny nodepool with label `prewarm=true` and no `spot` flag. then kustomize or patch the podSpec to tolerate `prewarm=true` only for critical workloads. example patch:
```
kubectl label nodepool prewarm-pool prewarm=true
kubectl patch nodeprewarm prewarm-pool -p '{"spec":{"taints":[]}}'
```
(rough, adapt to GKE nodepool API)

maria: also double-check SNAT usage — when CA spins many nodes they all pull images and hit the NAT gateway. we had transient 100% SNAT ports 2 weeks ago which made kubelet pulls timeout => node never registers. if SNAT exhausted you get the exact symptom.

elaine: good catch. grafana shows NAT port saturation spikes aligned with the node churn.

samir: OK action list: 1) bump `--max-node-provision-time` to 10m in staging CA, 2) create a 3-node prewarm (non-spot) pool with label `prewarm=true` and short-lived autoscaling, 3) increase NAT gateway port pool in asia-south1 (or move pulls through a regional registry proxy), 4) enable a soft-eviction-slope in autoscaler (experiment) to avoid immediate scale-in during jitter.

ops-bot: scheduled: CA config canary deploy to staging at 2026-06-04T04:30Z by @samir :white_check_mark:

kai: for the soft-eviction-slope idea — we can tune the CA to prefer nodes with longer lifetime estimates and avoid reacting to a single eviction event. i'll sketch a proposal in the infra runbook.

maria: I'll run a SNAT load test on a staging cluster and verify port capacity. if that's the blocker we can add an egress-GCLB nat or increase SNAT per nodepool.

sre-oncall: propose we roll the prewarm + CA bump to us-central1 first as a safety canary, then to asia-south1 during a low-traffic window. keep automatic rollback.

elaine: sounds good. i'll open the CA PR and the prewarm pool terraform change. will drop the PR links here when ready. thanks y'all :relieved:

samir: thx — ping when PR live and I'll run the staging canary validation.

elaine: PRs: https://git.internal/r/infra/ca-bump and https://git.internal/r/infra/prewarm-pool — tests running.

sre-oncall: noted. oncall will monitor preemptions and SNAT errors for 2 hours after canary rollout. :eyes:
